common_name: Rodeo Princess Daylily (2024 AHS Achievement Medal Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, average well-drained soil.

directions: Entered as three matching scapes before a panel of senior exhibition judges, Rodeo Princess won hybridizer Scott Elliott the American Hemerocallis Society's Achievement Medal in 2024 and was formally registered in 2025. It bears a light orange, 98-100% double self flower about 3.25 inches across on 31-inch scapes with five-way branching and roughly 26 buds, opening in the early season. Grow divisions in full sun in average, well-drained soil, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy bud count.
sources: Scott Elliott Daylilies & Maneki Hill Orchids cultivar catalog

common_name: His Royal Orangeness Daylily (2022 AHS Achievement Medal Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, average well-drained soil.

directions: Entered as three matching scapes before a panel of senior exhibition judges, His Royal Orangeness won hybridizer Scott Elliott the American Hemerocallis Society's Achievement Medal in 2022 and was formally registered in 2024. This unusual-form crispate daylily bears a bright light orange flower with a feathered red-orange eye (less prominent on the sepals) above an orange-green throat, about 6 inches across on evergreen 40-inch scapes with four branches and around 23 buds. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil, and divide every three to four years in spring to keep flowering vigorous.
sources: Scott Elliott Daylilies & Maneki Hill Orchids cultivar catalog

common_name: Scape Artist Daylily (2021 AHS Achievement Medal Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, average well-drained soil.

directions: Entered as three matching scapes before a panel of senior exhibition judges, Scape Artist won hybridizer Scott Elliott the American Hemerocallis Society's Achievement Medal in 2021 and was formally registered in 2024. This evergreen diploid bears a yellow flower with a dark reddish-brown eye, only faintly visible on the sepals, about 3.25 inches across on 25-inch scapes; the breeder has recorded as many as 108 buds on a single scape from its typical eight-branch, 73-bud habit. Grow divisions in full sun in average, well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring.
sources: Scott Elliott Daylilies & Maneki Hill Orchids cultivar catalog

This evergreen diploid bears a dusty rose flower with a dark red-purple band, about 2.75 inches across on 29-inch midseason scapes with two branches and roughly 22 buds. Grow divisions in full sun in average, well-drained soil, and divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Christmas Corsage Daylily (2021 AHS Achievement Medal Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, average well-drained soil.

directions: Entered as three matching scapes before a panel of senior exhibition judges, Christmas Corsage won hybridizer Heather Herrington the American Hemerocallis Society's Achievement Medal in 2021, the same year it was registered from a cross of Pea Green with Envy and Star Over Oz. This dormant rebloomer bears a brick cherry-red flower with a large olive-lime throat overlaid with iridescent maize brushing, about 5.75 inches across on 33-inch scapes with five-way branching and around 25 buds, opening early midseason. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring.

common_name: Dragonfly Derby Daylily (2021 AHS Achievement Medal Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun, average well-drained soil.

directions: Entered as three matching scapes before a panel of senior exhibition judges, Dragonfly Derby won hybridizer Heather Herrington the American Hemerocallis Society's Achievement Medal in 2021, the same year it was registered from a cross of Journey to Oz and Say Hello to Hans. This dormant rebloomer is an unusual-form crispate-cascade daylily with a peach, pink, and lavender blend flower showing a dark wine eye and neon lime-green throat, about 5.25 inches across on 33-inch scapes with five-way branching and around 25 buds, opening early midseason. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years in spring.
